article_title: A randomized controlled trial of a smartphone-based well-being training in public school system employees during the COVID-19 pandemic.
citation: Hirshberg Matthew J., Frye Corrina, Dahl Cortland J., Riordan Kevin M., Vack Nathan J., Sachs Jane, Goldman Robin, Davidson Richard J., Goldberg Simon B. (2022). A Randomized Controlled Trial of a Smartphone-Based Well-Being Training in Public School System Employees During the COVID-19 Pandemic. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000739
title: Healthy Minds Program (HMP) four-week smartphone meditation course
description: The Healthy Minds Program is a free smartphone-based meditation app constructed around the ACIP model. The four-week Foundations course studied here "includes two introductory audio lessons and two introductory guided meditations... followed by one week of content for each pillar of well-being," with two brief podcast lessons (5 to 7 minutes each) and three guided meditations per week. "In total, the intervention contains 10 lessons and 14 guided meditations." Participants choose between two guides, active or sitting practices, and practice lengths of 5 to 30 minutes, requiring only minutes a day.
requirements: A smartphone capable of downloading the HMP app
constraints: Participants with prior HMP use, meditation retreat experience, or a regular meditation practice were excluded from the trial
target_learners: Public school system employees (teachers, instructional, building, and administrative staff)
target_learning_goals: Reduction of psychological distress and training of awareness, connection, insight, and purpose skills
examples: Delivered remotely to 344 Wisconsin school system employees during summer 2020 or the first month of the school year, with automated REDCap reminder emails supporting download and use
key_sources: Hirshberg Matthew J., Frye Corrina, Dahl Cortland J., Riordan Kevin M., Vack Nathan J., Sachs Jane, Goldman Robin, Davidson Richard J., Goldberg Simon B. (2022). A Randomized Controlled Trial of a Smartphone-Based Well-Being Training in Public School System Employees During the COVID-19 Pandemic. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000739

article_title: Pedagogical agents communicating and scaffolding students' learning: High school teachers' and students' perspectives
citation: Sikström, P., Valentini, C., Sivunen, A., & Kärkkäinen, T. (2024). Pedagogical Agents Communicating and Scaffolding Students' Learning : High School Teachers' and Students' Perspectives. Computers and Education, 222, Article 105140. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2024.105140
title: Human–machine communication in instruction: applying human communication scripts and the relational/task-related framework to pedagogical agents
description: The article extends human–machine communication (HMC) theory to the instructional context, arguing that teachers and students apply human-to-human communication scripts when evaluating PAs, and that instructional communication's two dimensions — relational and task-related — structure expectations for PA behavior. It builds on the computers are social actors (CASA) paradigm, under which "people tend to apply the same social scripts to both computers and humans." The framework organizes PA design around communicational, pedagogical, and technological considerations.
requirements: PA communication should be adaptive, adequate, relational, and logical, as the article states
constraints: Findings derive from Finnish high school teachers' and students' expectations, not from observed PA use
key_sources: Sikström, P., Valentini, C., Sivunen, A., & Kärkkäinen, T. (2024). Pedagogical Agents Communicating and Scaffolding Students' Learning : High School Teachers' and Students' Perspectives. Computers and Education, 222, Article 105140. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2024.105140

article_title: The Effect of Authentic Problem-Based Vocabulary Tasks on Vocabulary Learning of EFL Learners
citation: Fateme Shir Mohammadi. (2017). The Effect of Authentic Problem-Based Vocabulary Tasks on Vocabulary Learning of EFL Learners. International Journal of Education & Literacy Studies, 5(3). https://www.ijels.aiac.org.au
title: Hmelo-Silver's four-step PBL implementation model applied to vocabulary tasks
description: The article used Hmelo-Silver's (2004) model for practical implementation of PBL. As printed, "the learning process begins by exposing a real-life problem to the students, generating hypothesis about the problem, application of hypotheses to check them, reapplication after amendment (through peer and tutor feedback)". The researcher extracted the teaching method from this model plus constructivism and Bloom's higher-order thinking, and designed the problem-based vocabulary tasks based on it.
requirements: A real-life problem must be exposed to students to start the process
Peer and tutor feedback must support amendment and reapplication
constraints: The article states availability of problem-based materials for language classes and a step-by-step procedure for PBL in language classes were limiting issues the researcher had to overcome by designing tasks herself
examples: In session two, learners received a scenario about dripping taps, generated hypotheses in groups of 2 to 3, searched online for needed words, created conversations, and revised them after teacher and peer evaluation
key_sources: Fateme Shir Mohammadi. (2017). The Effect of Authentic Problem-Based Vocabulary Tasks on Vocabulary Learning of EFL Learners. International Journal of Education & Literacy Studies, 5(3). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1154085

article_title: Subjective learning gain from a simulation-based health management course: a mixed methods study.
citation: Gu Ren-Ping, Zhao Fang, Bai Jie, Sun Shan-Shan, Zhu Ai-Yong. (2024). Subjective learning gain from a simulation-based health management course: a mixed methods study. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2024.1400135
title: Health Management Scenario Simulation (HMSS) system for practicing the full health management process
description: The HMSS is a computer-based simulation in which students "act[] as community health managers" managing simulated residents with chronic diseases. After selecting a disease, the system draws a case from a patient database and poses sequential questions across health service process modules; the system "generated a raw score based on the correctly chosen relevant items." Students explore health risks, provide guidance, develop intervention plans, arrange follow-ups, and collaborate with institutions.
requirements: Students work through all health service process modules of a case before completion
Cases are drawn from a patient database after selecting a specific chronic disease
constraints: The authors state the HMSS's function needs further expansion in terms of knowledge
target_learners: third-year undergraduate Bachelor of Health Management students
target_learning_goals: health management skills including information collection, risk assessment, intervention planning, follow-up, and emergency response
examples: In the studied course, groups of three students completed six case scenarios across two weeks, each case consisting of seven modules including health information collection, assessment, goal setting, intervention, follow-up, evaluation, and emergency response.
key_sources: Gu Ren-Ping, Zhao Fang, Bai Jie, Sun Shan-Shan, Zhu Ai-Yong. (2024). Subjective learning gain from a simulation-based health management course: a mixed methods study. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2024.1400135
